candidates.text: Brennan claims the Arcadia at 10:30 PM, which is when the fight card on the bar radio was on. Asked about it, Brennan cannot say that the challenger went down in the fourth and the crowd booed it — and everybody who was there can.
Tillman still carries it: candle smoke on the ceilings of everyone who sat it out. The fuse going in the building was at 9:00 PM, at the Hallam.
Found at the back lot: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Tillman, endorsed to Mulcahy, three months past due.
Coffin says Mulcahy told Tillman that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the Arcadia: A draft codicil in Mulcahy’s hand striking Moretti out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Callahan says Mulcahy told Moretti the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Found at the Hallam: A lease assignment made out in Brennan’s name, waiting only on Mulcahy’s signature.
Mosley says Mulcahy told Brennan the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Found at the back lot: A clipping about the failure of Mosley’s business, with Mulcahy’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Hanrahan says Mosley said Mulcahy had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Hauck hired us, and wants it known that Tillman owed the victim money, and would rather we started there.
Moretti on Tillman: Tillman’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Mosley on Tillman: Somebody at the chop suey place sells what a druggist will not, and Tillman knows which door.
Hanrahan on Tillman: Tillman was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at the chop suey place, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at the chop suey place signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at the chop suey place gives it up rather than be held: Tillman was there from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
The doctor Tillman used to see confirms the habit and the hour: Tillman was at the chop suey place from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, and could not have crossed the street unhelped.
Callahan on Moretti: Moretti had taken a drink and had gone to some trouble about the smell of it.
Mosley on Moretti: Moretti is on a temperance pledge that Moretti mentions before anybody asks.

A bottle at the Arcadia pushed behind the pipes, the seal broken and the level down.
A tab at the Arcadia in a name that is not Moretti’s, in Moretti’s handwriting.
The man behind the counter at the Arcadia knows exactly: Moretti was on the same stool from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM and was in no condition to walk anywhere, let alone do this.
The tab at the Arcadia is dated and timed, from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM, and Moretti was there to run it up.
